You think you know it all? Kevin Trudeau was once the same.

He says you have to be teachable. Kevin was taught to have a high teachability index: a willingness to learn and a willingness to accept change.

He meets people in their twenties who think they know everything. He admits he felt the same at 22 and 23, when the old guys seemed to know nothing. Now he's the old guy. His advice is to be an empty vessel, open to learning and change.

When did you last change your mind about something important?

Kevin's free training, Your Wish Is Your Command, is in my highlights.

#ad #success #mindset #kevintrudeau

Knowledge is not what wins. Tom Brady says so.

Kevin Trudeau shares a Tom Brady interview. A team with eight five-star recruits beat a team with fifty. Brady said the difference isn't the numbers. It's how a player handles adversity, like three interceptions in a row.

Kevin says the same is true of trading and of making money. Mental and emotional toughness decide the outcome, not knowledge. Your attitude, not your aptitude, determines your altitude.

How do you react when things go wrong?

Kevin's network for money and success thinking (GIN) is in my highlights.

#ad #success #mindset #kevintrudeau

Two railroads tried to crush Rockefeller. It made him richer.

Kevin Trudeau tells the story this way. The only two railroads carrying Rockefeller's kerosene teamed up and tripled their prices. He was almost broke and angry.

He walked his refineries and asked why oil needed railroads at all. It already moved through a pipe, so he built a pipeline across America, at about a third of what the railroads charged.

Kevin's point: the challenge held the seed of a greater benefit.

What setback could you turn around?
